items.title: The coinductive monoid of permutation trees is F-inverse
items.author: Antonio Bucciarelli; Arturo De Faveri; Giulio Manzonetto; Antonino Salibra
items.source_version: FSCD2026 LIPIcs378 article9, official CC BY4.0 publisher PDF; complete permutation-tree construction Theorem22 with Definitions12-14/19 and full author proofs15/16/18/20/21 pp9:8-9:10; necessary section2 conventions
items.difficulty_reason: The author constructs multiplication and inversion on possibly infinite permutation-labelled ordered trees by coinduction, proves E-unitarity, identifies the natural order structurally, and constructs a unique maximal representative by recursively removing fixed idempotent tails. The final F-inverse property uses a compatibility/minimum-group-congruence argument. These interacting coinductive and inverse-semigroup constructions support H2 as one main structural result, rather than counting its short final consequence or each support lemma separately.
